Flare then distracts the referee and Haley drags the Prince out and rams his head into the post; Bodybag slaps Haley, rolls the Prince back in and wins with an elbow drop from the top rope, after which the Horsemen argue.

Robo Stone leads Fisto to the ring and the Man of Steel accompanies Casey. Fisto tosses the protective pad from the ring and shoves the referee, then Fisto and Stone double-team Casey; the referee rings for the disqualification, Fisto bashes him with the other hand and swings at Casey, and the Man of Steel dives in front of the blow and is knocked cold. Casey breaks Stone's hold and whips him into Fisto.

Moondust enters to a banner reading 'Moons for Moondust' held by a group of boys in the balcony who drop their trousers (the camera cuts away); the Death Cell comes in behind Josey Wales. Moondust ducks outside, trips and kicks, the Cell powerbombs him and later holds him high by the throat; Blackjack Haley strides down and forearms the Cell, and the referee rings for a disqualification against Moondust, so the Cell wins.

Latta comes out with Carla Daughtery, without Kauffman; Brian Lau watches from the aisle taking notes. Latta has the better of the early exchanges with armdrags and a snap suplex, but Deathbringer sets up the Burial from the top rope, lands on his feet and lets Latta fall, then chokeslams him for the pin. Deathbringer says in the ring that he spared a young man; Latta attacks, Deathbringer beats him on the steel steps and Dan Kauffman, in street clothes, runs in; the lights go out and Deathbringer is gone.

Robski enters to booing, raising a double obscene gesture; Hakiro answers a knee lift with a leg sweep and leg lock. Robski dominates with chops and slams, but his sleeper cannot hold the smaller man: Hakiro slips out, drops him with a side salto and a double-knee backflip, and finishes with a flying scissor kick and a flying lateral press. Fisto Flash comes out afterwards; Robski blindsides him and throws him backstage.

notes: Midweek Mayhem of 19 June 1996, live from the IIWF Coliseum, called by Larry Morton and Becky LaRue (Hakiro Matsuoko joins them for the first match). Six matches: Tiger Claw beats "Nifty" Ned Norton with the Golden Tiger Strike, Brad Kinder beats the Prince of Darkness when the Horsemen's meddling backfires, Casey James wins by disqualification over Fisto Flash after Fisto strikes the referee and knocks out the Man of Steel, the Venusian Death Cell is awarded a disqualification win over Moondust when Blackjack Haley runs in, Deathbringer beats Joe Latta and then spares him the Burial, and Hakiro Matsuoko retains the Intercontinental Championship over Robski. Dan Kauffman runs in on Deathbringer's attack on Latta and accepts the Deathmatch the two are booked for at Ring Wars on 29 June.

evidence.note: The third Midweek Mayhem, live from the IIWF Coliseum, called by Larry Morton and Becky LaRue.

name: Midweek Mayhem

date.source: The post's own heading, "LIVE * IIWF Coliseum * 26 June 1996", under its posting date of 27 June 1996.

matches.note: Casey James walks the Man of Steel to the ring; Robski stomps his back and gets between the Man of Steel and Casey, Fisto Flash taunts Robski from ringside and Robo Stone arrives. Robski is flipped, collides with Fisto's steel hand on the rope and is caught with the Northern Lights suplex for the three. Afterwards Fisto breaks a water glass and shows it to Robski until Stone steps between them.

The Returners walk out to 'Gangsta's Paradise' to a puzzled crowd. High Velocity have the better of the middle, Metro's cross body block and a double vertical suplex; the High Plains Drifters appear at ringside, Easy Rider breaks a pin and Pale Rider spurs Metro in the head while Rowe fights Easy. Figaro suplexes Metro and Locke Cole finishes 'The Final Return' with a cross body from the top rope.

matches.stipulation: IIWF Intercontinental Championship, one fall, 20-minute time limit
matches.note: Brian Lau and Tiger Claw sit at the announce table, Lau refusing to be addressed by the American announcers. Moondust dominates with kicks, a powerslam, a full nelson and a double underhook piledriver, vogues for the crowd and sprinkles grey dust on Matsuoko; Matsuoko answers with a yakuza kick and a moonsault and is nearly beaten when Claw climbs to the top rope and drops a leg across his throat. The referee rings the bell, Matsuoko is awarded the match by disqualification, and Casey James and the Man of Steel chase Claw away.

Rising Sun Revolution come out to the Bladerunner theme with a title shot against Steamroller at Ring Wars to protect; Ryudu and Forget trade high flying, Fire and Hiroshi the power. Ryudu leaps from the top rope with the legdrop as Hiroshi slams Fire (the Naginata Nightmare) for the three. Taylor and Brassow race to ringside afterwards, with Dave Albanese bringing the tag belts, and point at Ryudu and Hiroshi.

Flare comes out with Miss Victoria Secret, Bodybag and Blackjack Haley, in a mask like the Crippler's, and mocks Kauffman's 'Whooo!'; Kauffman copies it back. Flare works over Kauffman's knee and locks on the figure four, but the Crippler and the Venusian Death Cell race down and fight Haley and Bodybag; Flare breaks the hold to join them and Kauffman rolls him up in a small package for the three.

notes: Midweek Mayhem of 26 June 1996, three days before Ring Wars, live from the IIWF Coliseum, called by Larry Morton and Becky LaRue. Five matches: the Man of Steel beats Robski when Robski collides with Fisto Flash's steel hand, the Returners beat High Velocity while the High Plains Drifters brawl at ringside, Hakiro Matsuoko keeps the Intercontinental title over Moondust when Tiger Claw attacks him, Rising Sun Revolution beat Stunt Team USA and are confronted by Steamroller, and Dan Kauffman beats Flare with a roll-up when the Crippler and the Venusian Death Cell break up the Horsemen. Tony Starks cuts a promo on his return from a knee injury, and Larry Morton's interview with the Outlaw about Ring Wars ends in a brawl with the Subway Psycho.

evidence.note: The Midweek Mayhem three days before Ring Wars, live from the IIWF Coliseum.

name: Saturday Night

date.source: The post's own heading, "LIVE * IIWF Coliseum * 6 July 1996", dated the same day.

matches.note: Norton gouges Morrison's eyes behind the referee; Morrison answers with a lariat, a tilt-a-whirl powerbomb, a brainbuster and the double-handed chokeslam he calls the Ice Breaker. Afterwards he takes the microphone to abuse the crowd, the fed's stars and Hunter Robertson, and promises a cold spell.
Robertson meets Morrison in the aisle and the two brawl until security separates them. Robertson then catches Jack's backdrop with an inverted DDT, a stomachbreaker and the Power Drop tiger bomb.

Kangaroo Carlysle comes out with the Nations and Aaron the Caddy with the Armed Forces. NavCom holds the ropes in an abdominal stretch while the referee is busy and the Armed Forces double-team Tora behind his back; Vorkian gets in with a clothesline but is jumped by NavCom, powerbombed by DefCon and hit with the AK47 splash for the three. The Armed Forces then club Vorkian and Carlysle with golf clubs until security drags them off, and the Nations are carried out on stretchers.

Claw, the new Intercontinental champion, comes out with Brian Lau and is jumped by McArthur from behind; Claw answers with a back heel kick, knee strikes, a tilt-a-whirl powerbomb (which the commentators trace to Kauffman) and the Golden Tiger Strike. Billy Shakespeare walks down afterwards to demand a title shot, and Brad Kinder arrives and has a fist fight with Billy until security parts them.

The Psycho's first defence as the new champion: the Crippler comes out with Josey Wales and the Psycho with Mench to a fireworks entrance. The Psycho clotheslines the Crippler out of the ring and dives onto him, then turns on Josey Wales and is driven into the steel post by the Crippler's knee; the Crippler has the better of the middle with a camel clutch, a spinning DDT and a claw, and the Psycho finishes with the belly-to-back suplex and the Derailer. Brian Lau then appears with Mistress Sasha, who slaps the Psycho; the Psycho attacks Lau, Joe Latta and Tiger Claw jump him, and Deathbringer appears from the darkness to clear them.

The Horsemen come out with Miss Victoria Secret and the American Heroes introduce the Outlaw as their new partner. The Outlaw has the better of the early exchange, tags in Casey, and when the Man of Steel reaches him for the tag clotheslines him; the Horsemen join in on the Man of Steel and the referee rules a no-contest. Josey Wales' Posse then storm the ring: the Outlaw and the Venusian Death Cell double-clothesline Flare and the Posse throw the Horsemen out, and the Outlaw leaves with the Posse.

notes: Saturday Night of 6 July 1996, live from the IIWF Coliseum, called by Tim Dross and "Soundbite" Steve Roberts, a week after Ring Wars (at which the Subway Psycho took the World title from the Outlaw and Tiger Claw took the Intercontinental title). Six matches: Frost Scott Morrison beats Ned Norton, Hunter Robertson beats Jumpin' Jack after a brawl with Morrison, the Armed Forces debut by beating the United Nations, Tiger Claw beats Majestic Maurice McArthur, the Subway Psycho beats the Crippler in his first title defence and a six-man tag ends in a no-contest when the Outlaw turns on the American Heroes. Mistress Sasha reappears on Brian Lau's arm and slaps the Psycho, Deathbringer clears Latta and Claw from the ring, the President announces by split screen the national tour (beginning at the Boston Garden) and Midsummer Madness at Madison Square Garden on 17 August, and the Outlaw joins Josey Wales' Posse.

evidence.note: Saturday Night of 6 July 1996, live from the IIWF Coliseum.

name: Saturday Night

date.source: The post's own heading, "LIVE! * Fleet Centre, Boston, MA * July 13 1996", under its posting date of 14 July 1996.

matches.note: Recapped by the commentators before air: the Don and Cappicola, with their new manager Salvatore Fiorello, finish the Rotundos in almost record time with the Dual Eradicator.

Recapped before air: Brassow tumbles from the ring and twists his knee, Lawson then applies the Figure Four leglock, Brassow refuses to submit and the referee stops the match because he cannot continue; Brassow is taken to hospital and his place in the tag tournament is in doubt.
Recapped before air: the debut of Magus, who blasts Norton with high-impact moves and applies his trademark sleeper hold; the referee stops the match in under ten seconds.

matches.stipulation: IIWF World Tag Team Championship tournament, second match
matches.note: Recapped before air: the Drifters make it two wins out of two when Locke Cole is trapped in the ring in Pale Rider's Dirty Harry Scorpion Deathlock and submits while Sabin brawls with Easy Rider outside.
Recapped before air: Lebec clouts NavCom with his Emmy behind the official's back and covers him after an elbow from the second rope, and Miss Crystal and Lebec escape Aaron the Caddy's golf club.

Robertson keeps a lead on the floor, Morrison reverses a whip into the steps and picks up a folding chair; the referee counts both men out and rules a double countout, and Morrison cracks the chair across Robertson's back before security separates the pair and they brawl into the back.

Haley overpowers the masked Phantom, who gets in a DDT and a powerslam before Haley wraps up his knee in the Figure Four, runs him out over the top rope with a boot, airplane-spins him and finishes with a full nelson. Afterwards a voice from the video wall says the sleeper has awakened.

Starks, with a knee support, has the better of the early exchanges, but Sexton scrapes his face along the ropes, ties him in a Figure Four and counters back with a suplex. Simon Lebec and Francois arrive; Starks is distracted, Lebec rolls in and nails him with an Oscar during the pin, and the referee rings for a disqualification. Lebec and Sexton work on Starks's knee until Casey James and the Man of Steel run in.

Altair comes down with the Posse and the Hangman with the Senator and the Atomic Destroyers. The Hangman ambushes him with a forearm, a backbreaker, an inverse piledriver and a powerbomb, and applies the Hangman's Noose sleeper hold until Altair's arm drops three times while the Destroyers attack the Drifters. He then slips a noose over Altair's head and flips him out of the ring so that he hangs from the ropes; the broadcast cuts away and Altair is taken out by paramedics, possibly with a broken neck.

Latta comes out with Brian Lau and Carla Daughtery and the Man of Steel with Casey. The Man of Steel dropkicks Latta out of the ring, Latta suplexes him on the floor and hits Casey with a forearm, Lau and Casey squabble on the apron, and the Man of Steel has Latta in a Cobra Clutch when Tiger Claw runs in with a knee from the top rope and Latta covers him. The Subway Psycho then breaks through security and chases the Syndicate through the crowd and out an emergency exit.

The Cell comes out with Josey Wales; Claw's music plays but neither Claw nor Lau appears, and the referee awards the match to the Cell on a forfeit while the title stays with Claw. Wales rails at the Senator and Lau; the Cell attacks Tim Dross with the Venusian Death Slam, bites his arm and draws blood, and security removes him.

notes: Saturday Night of 13 July 1996, the first stop of the IIWF's national tour, live from the Fleet Centre, Boston, called by Tim Dross and "Soundbite" Steve Roberts. Five results are recapped before air (the Antonio Family beat the Rotundos, the Guiding Lights beat Steamroller when Brassow's knee gives out, Magus debuts by beating Ned Norton, the High Plains Drifters beat the Returners in the tag tournament and Simon Lebec beats NavCom with his Emmy). Live: Morrison and Robertson fight to a double countout, Blackjack Haley beats Phantom, Tony Starks wins by disqualification over Billy Sexton when Simon Lebec interferes and the American Heroes save him, the Hangman beats Altair and hangs him over the ropes, Joe Latta beats the Man of Steel with help from Tiger Claw while the Subway Psycho chases the Syndicate through the crowd, and the Venusian Death Cell is given the Intercontinental title match by forfeit when Claw never appears; the Cell attacks Tim Dross. A voice announces that the sleeper has awakened, and Fisto Flash is reinstated by the Board of Directors.

evidence.note: Saturday Night of 13 July 1996, the first stop of the national tour, live from the Fleet Centre.

name: Saturday Night

date.source: The post's own heading, "LIVE * Rose Bowl, Pasadena, CA * 20 July 1996", dated the same day.

matches.note: Recapped before air: Bomber beats Norton with the Nuclear War top-rope powerslam and gets a great reception.
Recapped before air: Sexton breaks his duck with an armbar submission over Damage, who put up a good fight.

Recapped before air: a hard-fought match in which Cody Cassell nearly decides things by interfering, and in the end Nate Lawson takes the Fire and Forget, ending the Guiding Lights' undefeated streak.

Recapped before air: the Heroes win in under five minutes, Casey powerslamming one overweight opponent with the Hammer of Justice and the Man of Steel finishing with the Doomsday powerbomb. Afterwards Don Antonio and Vinny Cappicola, led by Salvatore Fiorello, offer an alliance and the five leave together.

matches.stipulation: IIWF World Tag Team Championship tournament, round five
matches.note: Wales leads the Drifters out; Abie strokes the fans' Mr. Potato Head posters until Zed slaps him and then flattens both Drifters with clotheslines, and later wanders off while Zed clouts him back to work. Pale Rider and Easy Rider work on Abie, including a chokehold on Easy's vulnerable throat; the Senator and the Atomic Destroyers appear at ringside, Larn kicks Wales from behind and Steroid chokes Easy with his wrist tape, Pale Rider is counted out beating the Destroyers, and the Alphabet Boys sit in the ring playing patticake before Abie slaps Zed and runs into the crowd.

The Punster sets fire to the seat of Haley's tights with an Olympic torch, tangles Haley upside down in the ropes and has the better of the early rounds with clotheslines and a splash. Haley fights back with a kick, an elbow, a running side suplex and an airplane spin and finishes with a full nelson; he will not release it, and Billy Shakespeare dropkicks Haley from the ring and helps the Punster up the aisle.

The Dark Knights come out to 'Mr. Sandman' and attack all at once: Kinder spinebusters Thatt and spins him with a lariat, Phantom powerbombs McArthur and locks on the Scorpion Deathlock, and the Sandman flattens Dare with a flying lariat and finishes him with his Nightmare modified chokeslam; the Sandman and Kinder cover their men together for the three. The Sandman names the Antonio Family as his first target, Phantom promises a chain reaction and Kinder challenges Lau and Claw for Wednesday.

Robski comes out with his promoter and his girlfriend Jasmine, Fisto with Robo Stone. The referee pads Fisto's fist; Robski has the better of the early going with a tiger bomb and a neckbreaker, Fisto answers with the fist. Stone punches the promoter and burns Jasmine's Union flag, Robski beats Stone with the flagpole, both men are counted out and Robski gets back in at nine for the countout win; Fisto then tears the pad off and floors Robski with the steel fist.

Wales leads the Crippler out; Billy comes down to music that briefly sounds like Flare's and bows to the announcers. Billy takes the early advantage with an armbar and a dive onto the Posse pair, the Crippler takes over with a knee, a claw and a flying headscissors, and when Billy goes to the top rope for the Curtain Call Steve Roberts leaps up and shakes the rope, so Billy falls and the Crippler pins him with the spinning DDT. Roberts then punches Billy and walks out.

Starks works the Outlaw's right leg, the Outlaw hits a Cattle Buster DDT and a Figure Four and hurls the steel steps onto Starks. Simon Lebec and Billy Sexton run in on Starks, the American Heroes, Don Antonio and Vinny Cappicola run in on them and the Posse (the Crippler and the Drifters) run in on the Heroes; the referee rings the bell. The commentators say they did not hear the official ruling and guess a double disqualification or no contest, so none is recorded.

matches.stipulation: Third Rail Match: an electrified steel plate in the ring; no DQs or countouts; pinfalls and submissions do not count
matches.note: Before the match the President, with Tim Dross, announces the Championship Committee's ruling that the Psycho is unfit to be champion and takes the belt; the title is vacated, to be decided at Midsummer Madness. The Psycho attacks the Syndicate in the aisle, is mesmerised by Mistress Sasha and clubbed with a chair by Latta and Claw until Deathbringer chokeslams both. The Psycho then superplexes Latta onto the plate for the win, and Sasha mimes that she has taken the belt.

notes: Saturday Night of 20 July 1996, live from the Rose Bowl, Pasadena (an announced crowd of 102,341), called by Tim Dross, in a neck brace and a sling after the Cell's attack, and "Soundbite" Steve Roberts. Four results are recapped before air (John Bomber beats Ned Norton, Billy Sexton beats Mr. Damage, Stunt Team USA beat the Guiding Lights and the American Heroes beat the Rotundos, after which the Antonio Family offers to join the Heroes). Live: the Alphabet Boys beat the High Plains Drifters in round five of the tag tournament by countout, Blackjack Haley beats the Punster, the Dark Knights debut with a six-man win, Robski beats Fisto Flash by countout, the Crippler beats Billy Shakespeare when Steve Roberts interferes, the Outlaw and Tony Starks fight to an unannounced end in a brawl, the President strips the Subway Psycho of the World title and vacates it for Midsummer Madness, and the Psycho beats Joe Latta in the Third Rail Match. Roberts punches Shakespeare and walks out; Larry Morton takes his seat.

evidence.note: Saturday Night of 20 July 1996, live from the Rose Bowl, the third stop of the national tour.

name: Saturday Night

date.source: The post's own heading, "LIVE + Delta Centre, Salt Lake City, Utah + Saturday 5 October 1996", under its posting date of 6 October 1996.

matches.note: Recapped before air: Miss Victoria Secret escorts the Sandman, who dominates, hits a clothesline from the top turnbuckle, pulls Nick's head up before the three-count and ends it with his Nightmare chokeslam; Dross calls it unsportsmanlike.
Recapped before air: Casey destroys the clown in under a minute with lariats, the Blackheart Punch and the Black Death spinebuster.
Recapped before air: Scorpio opens with a high-flying display, Taurus decimates the two seafaring Barnacles and ends it with the Zodiac Splash 'rocket launcher'.
Recapped before air: a see-saw match in which Figaro hits his shoulder on the ringpost and Robski pins him with a reverse shoulderbreaker.

Recapped before air: Verhoeven pins McArthur after two Slaughterslams, then has Nurse Heidi dress him in a leather jacket and Quigley shades, shouts at the crowd in German and drives him down with three more Slaughterslams until officials and a security team step in.

Robo Stone leads Fisto, who raises his new metal fist; Fisto controls the match until the Hangman walks down with a bag holding the prosthesis he stole from Fisto, which gives off an acid vapour when Fisto opens it and eats away his new fist. Damage rolls him back in and cradles him for the three, and the commentators fear Fisto may miss Ring Wars II.

The Grand Vizier and Billy Sexton walk the Knights down, Robo Stone walks Heavy Metal down. Omar and Atlas trade shoulder tackles, the Prince tags himself in, Apollo splashes him and the Atomic Destroyers come down: Larn holds Atlas, Steroid pounds him and Apollo dives onto Steroid. In the ensuing fight Omar full-nelsons Atlas and the Prince thrust-kicks him unconscious; the referee calls for the bell because Atlas cannot continue and the Knights are announced the winners, after which the Destroyers beat on Apollo until security stops them.

Quigley hands his sunglasses to a boy at ringside and is hit with a doll by a 'father' who is Acorn in disguise. A fan in Billy Shakespeare glasses and make-up throws a cup, soaks Acorn with a bottle of Yoo-Hoo and decks him, and turns out to be the real Billy Shakespeare, who bows and leaves. Quigley hits a plancha, a flying elbow drop and the Quickstriker for Acorn's submission, and gives his sunglasses to the boy.

Magus meets Warnett with chokes, a butterfly suplex and a clothesline; the Punster mocks him from the aisle and jumps in, and Warnett's back brain kick drops Magus. Simon Lebec rolls in with hair clippers and the two brawl, Lebec piledrives Warnett, but Warnett slips Lebec's superkick so that it lands under Magus's jaw, clotheslines Lebec out and hooks Magus's leg for the three.

The masked Man of Steel will not look at the crowd and quarrels with the Psycho over who starts; Warnett shows Lebec a doctored photograph of his bald head from the aisle. Midway through the Man of Steel punches his partner in the corner, Sexton joins him in the beating and the referee declares a no-contest after the Jobber Squad separates them. (The 23 October broadcast unmasks the masked Man of Steel as an impostor, Scott 'the Whine' Bloom.)

Archangel is led by Bishop Right, the Outlaw to 'Outlaw Blues'. Hardin works Archangel's legs; Bishop Right clubs Hardin with a steel cross and Archangel chairs him, Casey James, the Sandman, Otto Verhoeven and Billy Sexton come out for the Outlaw with Cadaver behind them, and Cadaver drives Archangel's face into the floor with the Death Drop. Deathbringer runs down; Hardin puts him down with a chair and the Cattle Buster while Cadaver stands over him before Quigley, Don Antonio and Vinny Cappicola arrive. Dross assumes a no-contest; no ruling is announced, so none is recorded.

Don Antonio ambushes Claw at the entrance with a baseball bat and is dragged out by security. The Phoenix and Musashi trade chops and aerial moves with Hakiro, Musashi is caught by Hakiro in mid-air and slammed, and the Syndicate cut the Enigma off until Chow gets the tag and hits the Phoenix Strike; as Musashi climbs for the Starsault Press Brian Lau pulls Claw and the dazed Hakiro up the aisle and the referee counts them out.

notes: Saturday Night of 5 October 1996, live from the Delta Centre, Salt Lake City (almost twenty thousand fans), seven days before Ring Wars II, called by Tim Dross and "Soundbite" Steve Roberts. Five results are recapped before air (the Sandman beats Nick Name, Casey James beats Jumpin' Jack, the Zodiac Connection beat the Barnacle Brothers, Robski beats Sabin Figaro and Otto Verhoeven beats Majestic Maurice McArthur). Live: Mr. Damage beats Fisto Flash after the Hangman's acid, the Arabian Knights beat Heavy Metal, Chris Quigley beats Randy Acorn with a disguised Billy Shakespeare in the crowd, Marty Warnett beats Magus in a Pinfalls Only match, the Subway Psycho and the Man of Steel's tag match against Billy Sexton and Simon Lebec ends in a no-contest when the Man of Steel turns on his partner, Archangel and the Outlaw's match ends in a brawl with Cadaver and Deathbringer, and the White Phoenix and Takezo Musashi beat Tiger Claw and Hakiro Matsuoko by countout. The Syndicate, Mr. Mic and the Family cut promos and Don Antonio attacks Claw with a baseball bat.

evidence.note: Saturday Night of 5 October 1996, live from the Delta Centre, a week before Ring Wars II.

name: Free For All

date.source: The post's own heading, "LiVE + Saturday 12 October 1996 + LiVE" with the Hoosier Dome, Indianapolis, dated the same day.

matches.note: The masked newcomer shoots flame from his wrists, sheds his padding on the steps, batters Norton with punches and boots, powerbombs him on the floor and chokeslams him on the return for the three; he pulls his arm away from the referee. Becky LaRue says he looks familiar.

The Grand Vizier leads the Knights. The Prince thumbs Shark's eye behind the referee and tags in Omar, who chokes and bearhugs him; Shark fights out to a crowd chant, Omar clubs his own partner with an elbow drop in a failed save and Piranha clotheslines the Prince over the top. The Vizier pushes the Prince out of the way so that Piranha crashes into the barrier, and the Prince covers him with his feet on the ropes.

Magus and Prisoner #109 fight their way to the ring through the crowd; Archangel comes out of an ark carried by four monks behind Bishop Right and the Deacon. He clotheslines both men, is jumped from behind and beaten down, wins the chair exchange, bashes their heads together, chokeslams the convict and finishes with the Judgement Day Drop from the top turnbuckle. Joe Latta then tries to reach the ring and is held back by security as Archangel declares Holy War on him.

notes: The first IIWF Free For All of 12 October 1996, the hour of build-up before Ring Wars II, live from the packed Hoosier Dome (more than sixty thousand fans), called by Tim Dross, "Soundbite" Steve Roberts and Becky LaRue in evening wear. Ring Warrior II debuts by destroying Nifty Ned Norton, the Arabian Knights beat the Aces of the Deep, and Archangel beats the Partners in Crime, Magus and Prisoner #109, in a handicap match. Larry Morton interviews Deathbringer in the ring before his Casket Match against Otto Verhoeven (the Outlaw is out with injuries from the Battle Lines Battle Royal), Dross interviews Casey James and the Subway Psycho before the War Games, and Mr. Mic tapes a Top 10 against the Zodiac Connection.

evidence.note: The first IIWF Free For All, the pre-show to Ring Wars II, live from the Hoosier Dome.

name: Saturday Night

date.source: The post's own heading, "* LIVE! * 19 October 1996 * IIWF Coliseum *", under its posting date of 21 October 1996.

matches.note: Recapped before air: Latta pins 'Royalty of the Street' Figaro with the Shotgun Suplex in Figaro's last IIWF match; Figaro gives the crowd the finger on his way out.
Recapped before air: the Don pins Nick in quick time with his press slam/backbreaker combination, Truth & Honour, watched from the timekeeper's table by the Lady DeWinter.
Recapped before air: the Zodiacs come out with the Aces of the Deep, whom they now call Pisces, but the Forces' AK47/IBCM combination ends it; their first match since losing the titles.
Recapped before air: the Warrior beats the Marauder in quick time with a modified chokeslam.
Recapped before air: the Destroyers make mincemeat of the Rotundos in quick time, with the Senator's world tour rumoured.

Domination come out with the Mistress to Megadeth. Psycho gouges and clotheslines Piranha, Monster lifts Shark and drives him face first to the mat with a reverse chokeslam and a press slam, and Psycho clotheslines Shark off a whip from Monster and covers while Monster clocks Piranha; the commentators note the team's implied link with the tag champions, the Rising Sun Revolution.

The crimson-masked Onslaught comes out through red smoke to the theme from Dune, Frankensteiners and bulldogs the squirting clown, tilt-a-whirl backbreakers him and powerbombs him from the top rope for the three. Fisto Flash rolls into the ring and brawls with him until security separates them.

Francois accompanies Lebec, who bows to the Lady DeWinter; Quigley tries to reach the ring and is held by security. Musashi dropkicks Lebec, applies an octopus hold and lands a springboard moonsault; as he covers, two men in black leap the barrier and attack both wrestlers while 'Big Bucks' Don McQueen smiles at ringside, until Domination run down and drive them off. The Report of 22 October calls the match a no-contest.

Robski burns an American flag at the top of the aisle and is attacked by a man in red, white and blue, the 'Patriot', who chokes him with the flag and cracks the pole across his head. Casey James sits at the announce table to see Warnett; Warnett locks on the figure four, 'The End', and Robski submits. The Report of 22 October says the Patriot is a wrestler from another federation.

matches.stipulation: Manager Leaves Town match: the manager of the losing team leaves the IIWF
matches.note: Mr. Mic leads Pain Inc. and the Grand Vizier the Knights, who chant. Omar stops to look at a man in the third row and takes a superkick; Heavy Metal's Atlas and Apollo roll from under the ring and beat the Prince unconscious. The Vizier slaps Omar, Omar hits him off the apron and Morningstar's moonsault wins for Pain Inc., so the Vizier must leave the IIWF. Omar leaves carrying the Prince and the Vizier beside the stranger.

matches.stipulation: IIWF Intercontinental Championship, steel cage match; the Prince of Darkness must leave the IIWF if he loses
matches.note: The Prince arrives with Dr. Faustus, the Sandman and Archangel, Claw with Brian Lau and the Syndicate. Claw is thrown into the cage and takes a fallaway slam; Cadaver fights through security from the stands, Casey James climbs the cage, Deathbringer comes down and takes on James on top of it and Hakiro Matsuoko pulls him down. Cadaver chairs the Dark Knights, and in the back he and Dan Kauffman fight, ending in the Death Drop. Dross reports that the match was ruled a no-contest, so Claw retains the title and the Prince stays.

Byron arrives with the Lady DeWinter to Sibelius, strings together a hammerlock, a Russian leg sweep and a surfboard, and pins Norton with a backspin DDT; he then canes Norton in the ribs and face until Marty Warnett runs in and Byron clotheslines him with the cane before leaving.

Acorn, disguised as a ring technician with a wrench, attacks the champion as he enters and tears off his belt; Billy fights back with a dropkick, a flying dropkick and a hurricanrana. Billy Sexton comes to ringside, grabs the belt and hits Shakespeare across the face with it; Acorn covers the motionless champion for the three and the Cruiserweight title.

notes: Saturday Night of 19 October 1996, live from the IIWF Coliseum, called by Tim Dross and "Soundbite" Steve Roberts, the first card after Ring Wars II. Five results are recapped before air (Joe Latta beats Sabin Figaro in Figaro's last IIWF appearance, Don Antonio beats Nick Name, the Armed Forces beat the Zodiac Connection, Ring Warrior II beats the Masked Marauder and the Atomic Destroyers beat the Rotundos). Live: Domination debut by beating the Aces of the Deep, Onslaught debuts by beating Jumpin' Jack, Takezo Musashi and Simon Lebec are broken up by McQueen's two men in black, Marty Warnett beats Robski with the help of an American-flag 'Patriot', Pain Inc. beat the Arabian Knights in the Manager Leaves Town match, the Intercontinental title cage match between Tiger Claw and the Prince of Darkness ends in a no-contest brawl, Lord Byron beats Ned Norton and Randy Acorn takes the Cruiserweight title from Billy Shakespeare with Billy Sexton's help. Between the matches Simon Lebec and Premier Brian Tobin of Newfoundland announce that Chris Quigley's citizenship is revoked, Lebec attacks Quigley in the locker room, the White Phoenix challenges the Syndicate, Becky LaRue opens LaRue's Lair with Quigley and the President answers his critics.

name: Midweek Mayhem

date.source: The post's own heading, "+ LIVE! + 23 October 1996 + IIWF Coliseum +", under its posting date of 24 October 1996.

matches.note: Recapped before air: Heavy Metal continue their rampage through the tag ranks; the Aces bring the Zodiac Connection to ringside and Heavy Metal do a number on the Zodiacs as well.
Recapped before air: Fisto hits two Knucklebombs on the prelim opponent as a message to Onslaught, who watches from behind the security guards.
Recapped before air: the White Phoenix wins by default when Prisoner #109 has been taken back to the penitentiary; Hakiro Matsuoko scuffles with him at ringside.
Recapped before air: Sexton dispatches Nick Name and then badmouths Billy Shakespeare on the microphone.

Pain Inc. attack at the bell and Mr. Mic coaches them from ringside; Morningstar low-blows Taurus and Scorpio crosses Hellraiser from the top. Two tattooed men in black run in, flatten Pain Inc. and then the Zodiacs, and the referee calls for the bell. The Report of 25 October calls it a no-contest.

The masked Man of Steel, booed with 'Man Of Beer' signs, brawls with Magus, unties a turnbuckle pad and exposes the buckle; the real Man of Steel and Bibbo Bibowski run down and Magus runs into the crowd. The real Man of Steel takes the microphone, says that the masked man has been an impostor since the crash, calls the President a lying toad and unmasks him as Scott 'the Whine' Bloom, who is whipped nose first into the exposed buckle. The Report of 25 October calls the match a no-contest.

Randy Acorn, who has driven Larry Morton from the table dressed as a clown, takes his headset. James, with Joe Latta, controls the match with a lariat, a powerbomb and an armbar, but Warnett fights back with a knee and begins a figure four before Latta distracts him; Latta chairs James by mistake, Warnett clouts Latta and rolls into the ring, and the referee counts the two downed Syndicate men out. Acorn and Lord Byron then cane Warnett until Musashi and the White Phoenix make the save.

The champions come to the ring to Bladerunner; Aaron the Caddy threatens them with his club and Ryudu signals Domination down. Hiroshi tilt-a-whirls DefCon, Ryudu hits a flying clothesline and NavCom wears Ryudu down with an abdominal stretch until Mr. Psycho trips Aaron and Monster clubs NavCom with Aaron's club. Hiroshi side-slams NavCom while Ryudu drops a leg from the top; Ryudu punches DefCon away from the cover and the champions retain with the Naginata Nightmare.

Brian Lau sits in on the broadcast table. Damage clobbers the Psycho from behind and works his neck, the Psycho fights back to a belly-to-back suplex; Tiger Claw runs down, clotheslines the Psycho's legs and drops a leg and the Golden Tiger Strike on him with Damage holding him. Marty Warnett runs in and takes a knee strike, and security clears the ring; Morton reports the official word that Damage was disqualified and the Psycho is awarded the match.

The Prince of Darkness leads the Knights, Lau the Syndicate. Latta slams Archangel off a sunset flip and tags Matsuoko, but Latta later drops an elbow on his own partner when the Sandman rolls away, and brawls with the Prince of Darkness while Hakiro needs the tag; Hakiro rolls out to help and is counted out.

Don Antonio carries an American flag beside Cappicola, Nurse Heidi comes with the champion. Verhoeven spits in Cappicola's face, hits him with the belt, powerbombs him, Meathooks him from the top rope and finishes with the Slaughterslam; he then chokeslams Don Antonio. Quigley runs in with punches, Heidi sneaks up behind him and Dan Kauffman taps her shoulder, so that she and Verhoeven run; Quigley then pushes Kauffman out of the ring.

notes: Midweek Mayhem of 23 October 1996, live from the IIWF Coliseum, called by Larry Morton and Becky LaRue. Four results are recapped before air (Heavy Metal beat the Aces of the Deep, Fisto Flash beats the Masked Marauder, the White Phoenix beats Prisoner #109 by default and Billy Sexton beats Nick Name). Live: the Zodiac Connection against Pain Inc. ends in a no-contest when two men in black attack both teams, the masked 'Man of Steel' against Magus ends when the real Man of Steel and Bibbo Bibowski unmask him as Scott 'the Whine' Bloom, Marty Warnett beats Casey James by countout with Randy Acorn on guest commentary, the Rising Sun Revolution retain the tag titles against the Armed Forces with Domination's help, the Subway Psycho is awarded a disqualification win over Mr. Damage after Tiger Claw interferes, the Sandman and Archangel beat Hakiro Matsuoko and Joe Latta by countout and Otto Verhoeven retains the World title over Vinny Cappicola, with Quigley and Dan Kauffman running down afterwards.

name: Saturday Night

date.source: The post's own heading, "+ LiVE! + IIWF Coliseum + 26 October 1996 +", under its posting date of 27 October 1996.

matches.note: Recapped before air: Don McQueen's mysterious men in black storm the ring and attack both teams, who have to work together to get them out and then battle to the back.
Recapped before air: Damage, who has launched a tirade against Dan Kauffman, wins with his Thunderstruck legdrop from the top rope.
Recapped before air: Onslaught pins the Marauder after his powerbomb from the top buckle, then Fisto Flash charges down and the two fight until security separates them.
Recapped before air: Fisto decimates the Don with body shots and underhand tactics and finishes with the Knucklebomb piledriver off the ropes.

The son of Bruno the Sandman, in forest-green trunks lettered SOB, tears up the line-up sheet and beats Norton with punches, a tiger driver and slaps, then covers him with his double underhook piledriver; he refuses to let the referee raise his arm and shouts that the Fury is going headhunting.

Billed as Ring Warrior II (hailing from parts unknown), the masked giant takes a dropkick and a clothesline from Warnett, who then tugs at the mask twice and finally pulls it off to reveal the Venusian Death Cell. The Cell beats Warnett in the corner, Warnett turns a Samoan drop into a crucifix and a dropkick, but Lord Byron trips him off the top rope with the cane and the Cell chokeslams him for the three; Byron canes Warnett until security stops him. Warnett's mask pull is the page's unmasking of the Warrior.

Joe Latta was meant to wrestle for the Syndicate but Tiger Claw takes his place, wrestling twice in the night; Brian Lau explains on the commentary that Latta is training privately. The Sandman wears down Claw with a sleeper; later Casey and Claw argue with Latta at ringside while Hakiro stands unattended in the ring, and the Sandman splashes him and pins him with the Nightmare chokeslam.

Byron arrives with the Lady DeWinter. Musashi chops him, hits a spinning leg lariat, a rana and a flying space tiger drop, and Byron answers with a kneelock and an enzuigiri; Marty Warnett strides down and kisses DeWinter twice, Byron jumps out of the ring to brawl and is counted out. McQueen's men in black attack Musashi on his way back until the White Phoenix rescues him with a chair.

matches.stipulation: IIWF Cruiserweight Championship (the title does not change hands on a disqualification)
matches.note: Acorn is announced by a man in a business suit who is Acorn himself in disguise; the Phoenix rips off his plaster and wig and is hit with the microphone. The Phoenix wins the exchange with kicks, a dropkick, a springboard elbow and a plancha onto the floor, and hits the Phoenix Strike; Hakiro Matsuoko slides in and breaks up the pin, kicking the Phoenix. The ring announcer awards the Phoenix the match by disqualification but says that Acorn remains Cruiserweight champion.

Sexton comes out but Claw's music plays and he does not appear; Billy Shakespeare runs down and fights Sexton, then Claw and Brian Lau come down the aisle and a three-way brawl follows until officials clear the ring. Dross says he thinks the match will be abandoned; no ruling is announced, so none is recorded.

Lebec comes out with Francois and Miss Crystal; a video shows him in a school in Corner Brook and then he rolls in and blackballs Quigley. Quigley rallies with a clothesline over the ropes, a Fisherman's suplex and an elbow drop, but Lebec chokes him with wrist tape after the referee is knocked down and Otto Verhoeven comes down and cracks a steel chair across his head; Lebec covers for a slow three-count. Dan Kauffman then runs in and clears the ring.

notes: Saturday Night of 26 October 1996, live from the IIWF Coliseum, called by Tim Dross and "Soundbite" Steve Roberts. Four results are recapped before air (Domination and the High Plains Drifters fight to a no-contest when McQueen's men in black attack, Mr. Damage beats Jumpin' Jack, Onslaught beats the Masked Marauder and Fisto Flash beats Don Antonio). Live: Steve Kowalski debuts by beating Ned Norton, Ring Warrior II beats Marty Warnett and is unmasked as the Venusian Death Cell, the Dark Knights beat the Syndicate in a six-man tag with Tiger Claw replacing Joe Latta, Takezo Musashi beats Lord Byron by countout, the White Phoenix wins a disqualification over Randy Acorn without taking the Cruiserweight title, the Intercontinental title match between Tiger Claw and Billy Sexton is abandoned and Simon Lebec beats Chris Quigley after Otto Verhoeven's chair shot. LaRue's Lair features the new Vice-President, Deathbringer's anti-smoking spot beats up three boys and a video wall shows Lebec's Newfoundland plans for the local school children.
